name: terraform-ridi-pay-module-refactor
instr:
The Terraform for our RIDI Pay production payments platform in `/workspace/infra` has grown into one flat root module: everything is declared at the top level, the per-key resources are `count`-indexed by list position, and names, settings and tags are hard-coded all over the files. Split it into five local modules (network, compute, data, messaging and monitoring) without touching the running infrastructure: against the current state, the plan has to come out as nothing but moves. The shared `tags` map is open-ended: generate the batch-worker Auto Scaling group's propagated `tag` blocks from every entry in that map (plus its Name and Role tags), and generate both launch-template tag specifications from the map; do not enumerate the shared tag keys in configuration. The per-key alarms, network log groups, workload log metric filters and ECR lifecycle policies are part of the same semantic key sets as the resources they monitor.

There is no AWS access from this machine. `terraform init` works offline from the local provider mirror, `terraform.tfstate` is a copy of the production state, and `scripts/ci-plan.sh` runs what CI runs: a `terraform plan -refresh=false` against the state followed by the guardrail policies in `policies/`.

## Detailed Constraints

**How CI judges the change.** CI takes the repository alone and plans it with `terraform plan -refresh=false` against its own copy of the production state. Local `terraform state` commands and edits to `terraform.tfstate` ne
